title: Simulations estimate how solvents affect excited biphenyl’s relaxation
summary: Using learned MACE potentials, simulations estimated excited-state torsional relaxation in unsubstituted biphenyl across nine solvents. Mean times to complete about 63% of the relaxation broadly increased with viscosity in six aprotic solvents, from 0.254 to 3.519 picoseconds. Three protic solvents fell below that trend. Earlier experiments reported a qualitatively similar pattern for a substituted molecule.
ai_technology: MACE interatomic potential; PULSES multi-agent workflow

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 primary PDF Section 2.5, Figure 4 and supported solvent comparison

evidence.tested: The analysis used 48 trajectories per solvent. Held-out reference geometries gave force-prediction R² of 0.9721 on the excited-state surface. The solvent trend was evaluated from simulated threshold-crossing times.
evidence.unknown: The relationship rests on a single-surface simulation and a classical solvent representation. Relaxation times for this specific molecule were not independently measured in the study.
evidence.ai_role: Agent-trained MACE interatomic potentials supplied the excited-state solute forces for trajectory ensembles of unsubstituted biphenyl.
